solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Suave and refined socialite who floats around?

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young society woman making her debut
something floating around is borne on the air

explanation.surface: A polished society figure who seems to drift through every party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' is a link word; the question mark admits that 'floats around' for 'on air' is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a debonair person is urbane, charming and polished in manner.

clue.text: Still time to ride competitively

parts.note: even can mean still, as in 'even more' or 'still more'

explanation.surface: There is still time to enter a riding competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb about time; it gives EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is the equestrian sport of dressage, cross-country and jumping, so to compete in it is to ride competitively.

clue.text: Nimrod confused with Ravel in fluvial song

indicators.note: the two composers' names are confused, mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Elgar's Nimrod gets muddled with Ravel in some river-themed piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Nimrod is a movement of Elgar's Enigma Variations, so the surface is all classical music; 'with' just joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Show Boat number about the Mississippi is a famous song about a river.

clue.text: Letter from girl on a return

indicators.note: on a return, the girl, 'on' and 'a' are read backwards together, as in a down clue going back up

parts.note: Margo is a girl's name
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A letter arrives from a girl, sent on a return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reads like a postal reply but signals that the whole run of pieces is turned backwards; 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerogram is a lightweight air-mail sheet that folds into its own envelope, a kind of letter.

clue.text: Conrad's story bizarre about spoil in old county

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the word for spoil
a bizarre version of the words is a strange rearrangement of their letters

parts.note: the name with its S used as a letter
to mar is to spoil

explanation.surface: Joseph Conrad wrote some strange tale set in a former county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarre' scrambles the fodder into ROSSANDCROTY, and 'about' wraps that round the word for spoil. It was a county in the far north of Scotland until 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a Scottish county abolished in local government reorganisation, so it is now a former one.

clue.text: Anger appropriate to principal motorway an illusory thing

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first and main motorway, read as MI
rage is anger

explanation.surface: Road rage on the M1 seems hardly real.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, London to Leeds, is Britain's principal motorway, with the 1 read as the letter I; 'appropriate to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mirage is an optical illusion, something seen that is not really there.

clue.text: Country mum's first rule?

parts.note: ma is mum, with the 's as 'is'
a law is a rule
I is the Roman numeral one, so first

explanation.surface: A mother's first rule of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first rule' reads as LAW I, a numbered law, with the order of the words swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in south-east Africa, an example of a country.

clue.text: Carry, pass, score

definitions.meaning: to carry a story in a paper is to print it
to pass, as a road or line passes along, is to extend or go along
in cricket a single scored is a point made by the batsmen

explanation.surface: Three verbs from sport: carrying the ball, passing, scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: a newspaper prints a piece, a road extends somewhere, and a cricket batsman scores a point between the wickets.

clue.text: Syrup of pineapple to store at home

indicators.note: the bomb is made to store, hold inside it, the word for at home

parts.note: pineapple is old military slang for a hand grenade
in means at home

explanation.surface: A sweet syrup made from pineapple, kept at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pineapple' pretends to be a fruit flavour but is a grenade.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet red pomegranate cordial used in cocktails, a kind of syrup.

clue.text: Drinking session ale knight and duke swallowed

indicators.note: the drink has swallowed, taken in, the two noble letters

parts.note: ale is a beer
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight and a duke down plenty of ale on a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' fits the drinking scene but puts N and D inside BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: going on a bender means a long bout of heavy drinking.

clue.text: Variable indefinite number triples? That's an irritation

indicators.note: variable letters can change, so they are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: n stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Maths jargon about variables and triples turns out to be a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variable' and 'indefinite number' look like algebra; one is the anagram signal and the other gives N. 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliver of wood stuck in the skin is a classic small but persistent irritation.

clue.text: Constant smoker worried about gas inhaled

indicators.note: the gas is breathed in, so it goes inside the turned word
about signals that the word is turned round

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried
N is the symbol for nitrogen, a gas

explanation.surface: A chain smoker frets about inhaling fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ATE to ETA, and 'inhaled' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a Sicilian volcano almost always emitting smoke, so it is jokingly a constant smoker.

clue.text: Large egg was broken by Scotsman — one from Govan?

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reassembled like a cracked egg

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A big egg was cracked by a Scot from Govan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' scrambles L, EGG and WAS into GLASWEG; 'by' sets IAN beside it. Govan is a district of Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Govan lies within Glasgow, so a person from there is a native of that city.

clue.text: She has it good — to thrash soldier we have on both sides?

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
our things are what we have
GI is an American soldier
R and L stand for right and left, both sides

explanation.surface: Someone seems to have done well thrashing a soldier who has us on both flanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition is sex appeal, an old sense ('the It girl').
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up or model known for her allure is a woman with 'it', that indefinable sex appeal.

clue.text: One excessive fellow into fruit

indicators.note: the fellow goes into the fruit

parts.note: a gourd is the fruit of a climbing plant
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A greedy man who is really into his fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like 'keen on' but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A glutton who eats too much is excessive at the table.

clue.text: Respectful expression where I see bacon cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are changed, like food in the pan

explanation.surface: A reverent remark from someone watching bacon fry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bow or curtsy expressing deference is a gesture of homage.

clue.text: Surrounded by morning papers?

parts.note: a.m. means morning
ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone buried in the morning newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' looks like newspapers but means identity documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: amid means among, in the middle of things around you.

clue.text: Choose tenor before getting involved with a show such as this

indicators.note: the word for before gets involved with, goes in among, the first letters

parts.note: to opt is to choose
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Pick a tenor first before getting caught up in a musical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting involved with' puts ERE inside OPTT; 'such as this' points to the clue's own theatrical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A light opera with songs and spoken dialogue is a kind of stage production.

clue.text: Fuel taken from under vans

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Fuel siphoned from beneath parked vans.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is the British term for diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is diesel oil used in road vehicles, a type of fuel.

clue.text: Soviet includes test given rocket

indicators.note: the Soviet word includes, holds inside, the test

parts.note: a red is a communist, a Soviet
to prove is to test, as in 'the exception proves the rule'

explanation.surface: The Soviet space programme tests a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocket' looks like a missile but in British slang to give someone a rocket is to tell them off severely.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being given a rocket means receiving a sharp rebuke, being scolded.

clue.text: Maybe Oxbridge man in team

parts.note: Oxford or Cambridge is an example of a university, a uni
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: Perhaps a Cambridge graduate plays in the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Many football clubs are called United, such as Manchester or Leeds, so it names a team.

clue.text: More on star from me?

indicators.note: the letters are made from the words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A stargazer promising more information about a star.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: someone who studies stars could tell you more about one.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies celestial bodies would be the source of further facts about a star.

clue.text: Flower came up

definitions.meaning: a bloom with thorny stems, the emblem of England
the past tense of a verb meaning to ascend or get up

explanation.surface: A flower came up in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a well-known garden bloom, and the past tense of the verb meaning to ascend.

clue.text: Saint suffering in Catholic country

parts.note: pain is suffering

explanation.surface: A saint suffering martyrdom in a Catholic land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' wants to be an anagram signal for SAINT; it is PAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is historically a strongly Roman Catholic nation.

clue.text: Forefather catching cold, one Greek sage at Troy

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: the pair are catching, taking in, the cold letter

parts.note: Nestor was the wise old counsellor of the Greeks at Troy

explanation.surface: An old ancestor caught a chill, like Nestor at the siege of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching cold' reads as falling ill but puts C into ANESTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a forebear from whom one is descended.

clue.text: English character in Greece gets leggy bird

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An Englishman in Greece meets a long-legged bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter, not a person; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless Australian bird has notably long legs.

clue.text: Joke playfully accepted by chess champion loyal to group

indicators.note: the joke is accepted by, taken inside, the champion

parts.note: Mikhail Tal was world chess champion in 1960
to rib someone is to tease them good-naturedly

explanation.surface: A world chess champion takes a joke well and stays loyal to his circle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tal is a crossword favourite among chess champions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal loyalty means fierce allegiance to one's own clan or set.

clue.text: Greatly productive association of states fills money reserve

indicators.note: the association fills, goes inside, the reserve

parts.note: a fund is a reserve of money
EC is the European Community

explanation.surface: A union of states tops up a cash reserve with fruitful results.
explanation.walkthrough: The European Community was the forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: fertile, highly fruitful and producing in abundance.

clue.text: In Argyle knit the makings of a jumper?

indicators.note: knitting works the letters together into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Knitting an Argyle-patterned sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater (Argyle is a diamond knitting pattern) but is a horse that jumps fences.
explanation.definitionFit: A year-old horse may grow into a steeplechaser, so it is potential raw material for a racing hurdler.
